Tell Me What I'm Missing

Give it a plan, decision or idea. Its job is not to praise you. Its job is to find the holes.

What it does

It challenges your assumptions, identifies missing information, surfaces risks and points out what you may have stopped questioning because you already like the idea.

When to use it

  • Right after you've decided something and feel great about it.
  • Before you take a plan to anyone who can say no.
  • When everyone you've asked agrees with you.

What to give it

  • The plan, decision or idea. A few sentences is enough.
  • What you're hoping the answer is. Be honest.

What you get back

  • The three assumptions most likely to make it fail.
  • The information you don't have yet.
  • The risks you've been skating past.
  • What evidence would change the conclusion.

How I actually use it

Make AI argue against the decision you've already made. This has become one of my favorite uses of AI because—shocker—I can become very attached to my own idea.

Assume I'm wrong. Find the three assumptions most likely to make this fail. Tell me what evidence would change your conclusion.
